entities.summary: Thomas Lee Flanagan was an American jazz pianist and composer. He grew up in Detroit, initially influenced by such pianists as Art Tatum, Teddy Wilson, and Nat King Cole, and then by bebop musicians. Within months of moving to New York in 1956, he had recorded with Miles Davis and on Sonny Rollins' album Saxophone Colossus. Recordings under various leaders, including Giant Steps of John Coltrane, continued well into 1962, when he became the full-time accompanist to Ella Fitzgerald. He worked with Fitzgerald for three years until 1965, and then in 1968 returned to be her pianist and musical director, this time for a decade.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a pianist and composer for Ella Fitzgerald, Flanagan contributed to her iconic recordings of the 1960s, including 'Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Cole Porter Songbook,' which remains a benchmark for jazz vocalists. His work with Fitzgerald helped preserve the legacy of bebop and swing music.
